subject: Re: Benchmark methodology follow-up: performance SLO qualification
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgefin.com>
Date: 2027-04-25 09:12 -07:00
Subject: Benchmark methodology: follow-up from demo

Hi Marissa / Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo today — the latency numbers looked promising. As a next step the engineering team here wants to validate performance against our SLOs before we move toward a pilot. Can you share:

- Your benchmark methodology (how you measure latency: p50/p95/p99, streaming vs batch)
- The prompt sets and eval harness you use so we can reproduce locally
- Definitions for throughput (tokens/sec), concurrency, and what counts as a warm vs cold cache
- Any requirements for the test environment (network egress, regions, GPU types)

Attached is our current load profile CSV and a short doc with our target SLOs:
- p95 latency (end-to-end streaming partial-token) <= 50ms
- sustained throughput 2000 tokens/sec with 8 concurrent streams

Can you also confirm whether Redwood supports streaming partial tokens (we need low tail latency) and whether KV cache pre-warm is possible for these runs?

Best,
Samir
Lead Architect, EdgeFin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@edgefin.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25 11:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology: follow-up from demo

Hi Samir / Priya — great to chat this morning. Recap + proposed next steps below.

Call recap (high level):
- EdgeFin target: p95 streaming tail <= 50ms, 2000 tokens/sec sustained at 8 concurrent streams
- Redwood showed a streaming-optimized runtime with prefix KV caching and configurable batching policies

What I attached:
- redwood_benchmark_harness_v1.zip (test harness, measurement scripts, and config templates)
- prompt_set_edgefin_v1.jsonl (sample prompt set derived from your example prompts)

Measurement definitions (how we run and report):
- Latency: measure both token-level emit latency (time from model token generation to first byte of stream) and request end-to-end latency. Report p50/p95/p99 for both.
- Throughput: measured as tokens/sec observed at the client during steady-state (after warmup window).
- Concurrency: number of simultaneous streaming sessions; we will run target concurrency and step tests (1/2/4/8/16).
- Warm vs cold: warm = KV cache pre-warmed for a given prefix set (we provide prefixes). Cold = empty KV. We specify warmup length (e.g., 5 min sustained).
- Reproducibility: harness includes Dockerfile + seed control for generation and a deterministic workload runner; we log environment (GPU type, driver, kernel) and store raw traces.

Ask from EdgeFin:
- Share a representative prompt set (if you want us to use different prompts than the attached sample) and your preferred test window (time/region).
- Confirm allowed test accounts and any egress constraints (we can run in us-west2 if that works).

Proposed next steps / schedule:
1) You upload final prompt_set_edgefin.jsonl and load profile CSV to the shared Drive link by EOD Mon (2027-04-26).
2) Redwood will prepare a sandbox deployment and run an initial baseline on Tue 2027-04-27 09:00-12:00 PT.
3) We’ll share raw traces and a short write-up within 24 hours and then sync to review results.

If the schedule works I’ll create the test run calendar invite and share the S3 bucket link for payloads.

Thanks — attaching the harness now.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Marissa — quick clarifications:
- Confirming we’ll upload our final prompt set by EOD Mon.
- For the streaming tail, when you say \"token-level emit latency\" do you instrument on the client side (time to first byte) or server side? We prefer client-side measurement but want to ensure clocks/sync are handled.
- Can you confirm whether KV cache pre-warm will be permitted on the sandbox (we can provide the prefixes).

Thanks,
Samir

On Apr 25, 2027, at 11:05, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26 11:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology: follow-up from demo

Thanks for the clarifying questions, Samir — good ones. Answers below and a couple of administrative items.

1) Token-level emit latency: we will capture both client-observed time-to-first-byte and server emit timestamps. For the official report we prefer client-side measurements (we provide a small sync routine in the harness to correct for clock skew). The harness logs both sides and includes a post-processing step to align traces.

2) KV cache pre-warm: yes — the sandbox supports pre-warm. Please provide the prefix list and we will run a 5-minute warmup prior to steady-state measurement. We’ll log cache hit rates as part of the run.

3) Test environment & region: we can run the sandbox in us-west2 (NVIDIA A100x2) — if you require a different instance class let us know and we’ll quote.

4) Administrative: I created the shared Drive folder and a read-only S3 bucket for payloads: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/edgefin/benchmark-plan-v1 — please upload prompt_set_edgefin_final.jsonl and confirm by replying. Also added the HubSpot deal (EDG-2027-0425) with the proposed run times.

Next actions (summary):
- EdgeFin: upload final prompt set + confirm bucket access (by EOD Mon 2027-04-26)
- Redwood: provision sandbox and run baseline Tue 2027-04-27 09:00-12:00 PT; share raw traces + summary within 24h

If you’re okay I’ll set the calendar invite for Tue morning.

—
Marissa
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
